I could be wrong, but I don't remember today's forecast calling for partly cloudy skies with a chance of fireballs.
What gives, Batman? What are these mechanized monsters and where did they come from?
They're Parademons, genetically modified soldiers from Apokolips. Which means Darkseid's invasion of the Earth has begun.
I'm still new to this superhero thing, but that sounds... bad. It's bad, isn't it?
It is if you value your free will. Darkseid intends to harness a power found on Earth to control the hearts and minds of the entire universe.
Okay, yeah, that's bad. Please tell me you have a plan.
I do, but we'll need to gather as many allies as we can to see it through.
If we can't find a way to unite and collaborate, the Earth is as good as doomed.
I've got good news and bad news, Batman.
The good news is we managed to track the Parademons back to the power plant.
The bad news is this wizard-looking dude was waiting for us there. Seems like he's gonna be trouble.
Must be Desaad, Apokolips' chief scientist, one of Darkseid's Elite, and a powerful psychic.
He'll likely try to debilitate us with his tech and psionics, so it'll behoove us to have means to counter them ready.
Fortunately, I anticipate his overreliance on both will leave him vulnerable to physical attacks. We should take advantage of that.
How do you always know all this stuff?
Actually, scratch that, I'm pretty sure I don't want to know.
There's no end to these Parademons! On their own, they're not so tough...
But every time I knock one down, two more seem to appear in its place.
You're not far off.  Parademons are capable of processing and repurposing organic material into new Parademons.
That if you don't want to end up becoming one of them, try focusing on attacks that can take out multiple Parademons at once.
You struggle in vain, Earthling. Lord Darkseid has conquered thousands of planets.
He has enlightened countless civilizations to the great darkness, granting them absolution and unity under his authority.
Do you, a primitive, truly believe you can stop him from claiming the Anti-Life Equation and taking his rightful place as the Supreme Being?
But you would be surprised what us 'primitives' can do when we unite. When we combine our strengths, we are mighty.
Mighty enough to even best a god? One capable of striking you down in a single blow?
Thank you all for your assistance thus far fending off Darkseid's forces.
Don't mention it. Rrreally, don't. We have rrreputations to maintain, afterrr all.
I realize we've had our differences in the past, but I hope we can continue to count on you in the battle against Steppenwolf.
We had little choice, didn't we?
If we'd left saving the world to the Justice League, we'd all be Parademons by now.
Yeah, and no one gets to enslave the Earth but us!
Now if you'll excuse me, I'm off to steal candy from a baby. All these heroics are grossin' me out.

1) Personal Battle Points - Your total Battle Points across all Areas, which unlock Personal Rewards.\n2) League Battle Points - The combined Battle Points of everyone in your League across all Areas, which unlock new Challenge Difficulties and higher tiers of rewards.\n3) Repel Damage - Your League's combined Battle Points in the Challenge Boss Area, which unlock Repel Rewards.

1) The challenge is divided into Areas, which may be composed of one or more Sectors.
2) When you fight enemies in a Sector, it increases its Stability.
3) You can only individually increase a Sector’s Stability by 10%.
4) Reaching 100% Stability in a Sector activates a Sector Skill.
5) Sector Skills can add to League Battle Points or deal Repel Damage to the Challenge Boss.
6) You can only help stabilize one Sector per Area, so you’ll need to coordinate with your League to efficiently split the work and reach 100% Stability in all Sectors.

1) You can unlock the third Area and battle the Challenge Boss starting at Challenge Difficulty 2.\n2) Battling the Challenge Boss and activating Repel Damage Sector Skills will fill the Repel Progress Bar.\n3) If your League can completely fill the Repel Progress Bar, all players will receive a boost to their Personal and League Battle Point totals.

1) Battlefield Buffs unlock at Challenge Difficulty 3.
2) Only the first two Areas grant Battlefield Buffs.
3) These buffs change each week but always give you an advantage against the Challenge Boss.
4) You can activate a Battlefield Buff by helping to stabilize its respective Area.
Relentless, seemingly endless waves of Parademons pour out of a boom tube. Parademons are the shock troops of Apokolips and must be confronted before they can can spread chaos throughout the city.

Assemble a team that can hit multiple targets or deal area of effect damage to effectively confront this grouped threat. Characters which gain bonuses when defeating an enemy will have more opportunities to trigger this effect.

The sadistic scientist and treacherous servant of Darkseid, DeSaad can inflict debilitating effects on his foes. He is, however, a craven and self-preserving coward who relies on technology over physical strength.

When you face DeSaad, you want a team with good defense against Power Damage, including Shields, and the ability to remove debuffs from your allies. Focus on dealing Physical Damage and, if you can, inflicting the Fear effect on DeSaad.
The general leading the military of Apokolips and one Darkseid's Elite, Steppenwolf is an immortal with vast strength, endurance, and speed with millenia of experience in the art of war and conquest.

Confront Steppenwolf with a team that can revive fallen allies, as his Ultimate will outright kill whomever it strikes. You will be even better prepared if the team you craft has better resistance to Physical Damage, focuses on Power Damage to side-step Steppenwolf's own Physical Resistance, and has strong ability to Block.
